journal_lines: §oSmelled the ore before any rock was visible — cold iron rising through the root system. Trees first, then stone.
§aRoots had grown deep into the seam. §lWoodcutter§a cut through. Miner reached what was underneath.
Three trees felled to expose the vein. The vein had been waiting a long time. Both bags earned.
§aTimber over ore — cleared the one to reach the other. The wood made the props. The props held the roof.
Felled, stripped, set, braced. Woodcutter built the support structure while the miner mapped the seam.
§aCut timber became the frame. §lOre§a came out through the frame. The same trees served twice.
§oSoil, then roots, then stone — all in an arm's depth. Took something from each layer on the way down.
§aCleared what the forest had built over the seam for years. Long day. Both came home heavy.
